cards.headline: Written before the script was finished
cards.snippet: In a 2016 Billboard interview after his Oscar nomination, composer David Lang said he wrote the operatic "Simple Song #3" before the script for Paolo Sorrentino's film Youth was finished. He worked from early copies of the script and dreamed about the emotional arc of Michael Caine's character and his life at the end. When he put questions to Sorrentino, the director would say he needed to cry. Lang felt the music revealed something about the character that the script or the acting couldn't reach.
cards.context: Billboard interview after the Oscar nomination.

cards.headline: Lang spilled coffee on himself at the nomination
cards.snippet: On Jan. 14, 2016, David Lang woke up to the Oscar nominations. His "Simple Song #3," written for the Michael Caine film Youth, was up for best original song. Lang, a first-time nominee, told Billboard he poured a big cup of coffee, turned on the Internet and watched the announcement. When his name was read, he spilled coffee all over himself.
